findings.reason: the deliverable must require the unchanged directories' recorded identities to be carried into the re-persisted shape, and the done-when needs a second cold read after a mutating build, or a stale-rows regression passes the gate unchallenged.
findings.text: §13's deliverable says an unchanged directory keeps its persisted *files* but never says it keeps its recorded *identity*, and each of the three cases reads once after one mutation, so nothing checks the shape the mutating build leaves behind: `build_index` persists `build.dir_stamps`, which it builds only from the `dirs` mapping it was handed (reckon/metadata_index.py:496-499), and it persists that map whenever the build changed (reckon/metadata_index.py:560-561), so an incremental build that hands `dirs` only the directories it scanned truncates the persisted directory map — and the reuse helper that reads it back checks only the directories it holds stamps for (reckon/metadata_index.py:401-408), so an unrecorded directory is read as unchanged and an HTML file added there is never seen by a later cold read

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited target resolves: `_walk_covered` (reckon/metadata_index.py:629), `_reuse_covered` (383), `index_rows` (334), `build_index` (468), `_served_index_rows` (reckon/serve.py:1189), `/ _index/<project>` (served at reckon/serve.py:2739), and `tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py` exists in `tests/`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — each case declares a control and the `os.scandir` spy is validated by case (1)'s control, but all three cases read once after one mutation, so the persisted shape a mutating build leaves for the next cold read (the unchanged directories' recorded identities) is measured by nothing.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs go "under the run directory with a revision header and ends in EXIT=", the same durable placement §7 and §12 use; nothing is placed in a session scratchpad or node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, filename or comment; the new file is named for its mechanism (`test_a_changed_directory_rescans_only_itself.py`), and the only numeric prose is a measurement (`2,514` directories, `9,983` files) that is evidence, not a code symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the Why's root cause matches its cited evidence (the py-spy trace in `_walk_covered` is exactly the walk the cold served read takes, verified at reckon/serve.py:1199-1205 and reckon/metadata_index.py:359-491); the mechanism produces each done-when (per-directory identity comparison yields one `os.scandir` on a non-covered add, and the covered set is a full walk's because `_dir_identity` (reckon/metadata_index.py:794-813) carries mtime/ctime/ino/size, all of which move on an entry add or remove); and the mechanism runs on the same code path the plan names — `build_index` is reached with `covered=None` by the production caller `_served_index_rows`, so no caller is left unnamed.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable (take the covered set from the persisted index and rescan only directories whose identity moved); the three cases are facets of that one measure, not separate deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §13 declares no `depends-on` and needs none (its `reckon/metadata_index.py` co-writer §3 is `done`), while its dependents declare the edge: `plan-section-depends-on` maps `s14`→`s13` and `s7`→`s13`, and §14's prose repeats "This runs after §13, which shares `reckon/metadata_index.py`".
